metadata.summary: England forward Owen Trout's one-month absence from Leigh Leopards matches last season was due to a ban after testing positive for cannabis.

The 27-year-old, who will join NRL side Cronulla Sharks from the 2027 season onwards, did not play for Leigh from May 16 to June 27 and the reason has now come to light following a statement from UK Anti-Doping (UKAD). Trout returned an adverse finding following a test after a match against Super League champions Wakefield Trinity in late March. The Yorkshireman was provisionally suspended on May 22 and admitted to smoking a joint and eating a cannabis gummy in the week leading up to the game against Wakefield. messages.text: Jones, Russell, Tuipulotu return in Scotland's quest for first win over All Blacks

metadata.summary: Gregor Townsend has welcomed back Huw Jones, Finn Russell and Sione Tuipulotu as Scotland seek a first-ever victory over New Zealand in Saturday's Nations Championship.
metadata.content: Nations Championship: Huw Jones, Finn Russell, Sione Tuipulotu start in Scotland quest for first-ever win vs New Zealand's All Blacks | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nations Championship: Huw Jones, Finn Russell, Sione Tuipulotu start in Scotland quest for first-ever win vs New Zealand's All Blacks Scotland face New Zealand on Saturday at Murrayfield (2.10pm kick-off), seeking a first ever win over the All Blacks; Centres Huw Jones and Sione Tuipulotu, and fly-half Finn Russell return to start; Scotland also face Australia (Nov 15) and Japan (Nov 21) this month Thursday 5 November 2026 14:22, UK Image: Huw Jones and Sione Tuipulotu are back starting together at centre as Scotland get ready to face the All Blacks on Saturday Gregor Townsend has welcomed back Huw Jones, Finn Russell and Sione Tuipulotu as Scotland seek a first-ever victory over New Zealand in Saturday's Nations Championship. Scotland's winless record against the All Blacks stands at 33 Tests, but a strong selection gives them hope ahead of the weekend's contest at Murrayfield (2.10pm kick-off). The backline sees a Jones-Tuipulotu British and Irish Lions centre partnership restored, with Russell guiding the side from fly-half. The latter is partnered by another Lion in scrum-half Ben White. Kyle Steyn and Jamie Dobie start on the wings, with Kyle Rowe at full-back, leaving Blair Kinghorn on the bench as a replacement.
